title: Attach scoped partner services
objective: Propose a services sequence for a workflow with poor content quality and low adoption readiness.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Partners add the most value when their services address what the customer's roadmap actually needs. Every service should have a clear causal link to a customer outcome.
Glean's partner-led services model has partners owning outcome delivery, rollout enablement, and change management. Glean retains governance, deployment quality, and technical authority.
Map the prioritized roadmap to the services it requires:

items: **Discovery facilitation**, to expand the Blueprint to new teams.

blocks.x: Define the outcomes, deliverables, responsibilities, assumptions, and exclusions in a scope that has been reviewed.
Scope is a framework, not a promise of everything

Glean's partner SOW template states that a package level is a sizing and delivery framework, not a commitment to connect every possible data source or deliver every identified use case. Discovery outputs don't authorize delivery work or set contractual terms.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't attach a generic services SKU unless it clearly causes the customer outcome.
Map each service to a need found in the Blueprint, so scope follows evidence.

blocks.title: Partner services mapped to Blueprint needs
blocks.alt: Six cards mapping partner services to the needs they address: discovery facilitation, deployment and connectors, agent design and implementation, adoption and change management, governance and knowledge readiness, and value measurement and optimization.
